title: Splitting a multilinear polynomial at half degree on the cube $\{1,\omega\}^n$
statement:
Let $K$ be a field, let $\omega \in K$ be nonzero, and let $(c_S)_{S \subseteq \mathrm{Fin}\,n}$ be a family of coefficients in $K$ indexed by the subsets of $\mathrm{Fin}\,n$. Then there exist polynomials $P_1, P_2 \in K[X_i : i \in \mathrm{Fin}\,n]$, each of total degree at most $\lfloor n/2 \rfloor$, such that for every point $x \in \{1,\omega\}^n$ (that is, every $x$ with $x_i \in \{1,\omega\}$ for all $i$),
\[
  \sum_{S \subseteq \mathrm{Fin}\,n} c_S \prod_{i \in S} x_i
   \;=\; P_1(x) + \Bigl(\prod_{i} x_i\Bigr)\, P_2(y),
   \qquad y_i = 1 + \omega^{-1} - \omega^{-1} x_i .
\]
hypotheses_covered: ω is a nonzero element of the field K
a coefficient family c indexed by subsets of Fin n
P₁ has total degree at most ⌊n/2⌋
P₂ has total degree at most ⌊n/2⌋
the identity holds for every x in the cube {1,ω}^n, with the argument of P₂ reparametrized coordinatewise by 1 + ω⁻¹ − ω⁻¹ xᵢ

   = P_1(x) + \Bigl(\prod_i x_i\Bigr)\cdot P_2\bigl(1 + \omega^{-1} - \omega^{-1}x_1,\dots,

\]
